```{r}
# -------------------- Step 1: Install and Load Required Libraries --------------------
# Install and load required packages
#install.packages("ggcorrplot")
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com/"))

if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) 

install.packages("ggplot2")

library(ggcorrplot)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------- Step 2: Load the Dataset --------------------
# Load the dataset
data <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\shara\\OneDrive - Indiana University\\Applied Stats\\hypothyroid.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# -------------------- Step 3: Select Relevant Columns --------------------
# Select relevant columns for analysis
selected_columns <- c("age", "sex", "T3", "TSH", "TT4", "FTI", "binaryClass")
data <- data[selected_columns]

# -------------------- Step 4: Inspect the Dataset --------------------
# Print column names
print("Selected columns:")
print(colnames(data))

# View the first few rows of the dataset
head(data)

# -------------------- Step 5: Replace Invalid Numeric Entries with NA --------------------
# Define numeric columns
numeric_columns <- c("age", "T3", "TSH", "TT4", "FTI")

# Convert numeric columns to numeric and replace invalid entries with NA
for (col in numeric_columns) {
  if (col %in% colnames(data)) {
    data[[col]] <- as.numeric(as.character(data[[col]]))
  }
}

# -------------------- Step 6: Replace Invalid Categorical Entries with NA --------------------
# Define categorical columns
categorical_columns <- c("sex", "binaryClass")

# Standardize and replace invalid categorical values with NA
for (col in categorical_columns) {
  if (col %in% colnames(data)) {
    data[[col]] <- tolower(trimws(data[[col]]))  # Standardize values
    data[[col]] <- ifelse(data[[col]] %in% c("", "?", "unknown"), NA, data[[col]])  # Replace invalid entries
  }
}

# -------------------- Step 7: Check for Missing Values --------------------
# Check missing values in each column
missing_values <- sapply(data, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
cat("Missing values count for each column:\n")
print(missing_values)

# -------------------- Step 8: Impute Missing Values --------------------
# Numeric columns: Replace NA with column mean
for (col in numeric_columns) {
  if (col %in% colnames(data)) {
    data[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(data[[col]]), mean(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE), data[[col]])
  }
}

# Categorical columns: Replace NA with "unknown"
for (col in categorical_columns) {
  if (col %in% colnames(data)) {
    data[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(data[[col]]), "unknown", data[[col]])
  }
}

# -------------------- Step 9: Save the Cleaned Dataset --------------------
write.csv(data, "C:/Users/penta/OneDrive - Indiana University/hideens/aapld stats/hypothyroid.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# -------------------- Step 10: Convert Categorical Columns to Factors --------------------
data$binaryClass <- as.factor(data$binaryClass)
data$sex <- as.factor(data$sex)

# -------------------- Step 11: Plot Visualizations --------------------
# Define a vector of distinct colors for histograms
colors <- c("pink", "green", "purple", "lightblue", "brown")

# Plot histograms for numeric variables
for (i in seq_along(numeric_columns)) {
  col <- numeric_columns[i]
  fill_color <- colors[i]

  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = !!sym(col))) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = fill_color, color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(title = paste("Distribution of", col), x = col, y = "Frequency") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

  # Apply x-axis limits only for the 'age' column
  if (col == "age") {
    p <- p + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
  }

  print(p)
}

# Define distinct colors for bar charts
colors <- c("blue", "orange")

# Plot bar charts for categorical variables
for (i in seq_along(categorical_columns)) {
  col <- categorical_columns[i]
  fill_color <- colors[i]

  c <- ggplot(data, aes(x = !!sym(col))) +
    geom_bar(fill = fill_color, color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(title = paste("Count of", col), x = col, y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

  print(c)
}

# Scatterplots for numeric pairs with binaryClass differentiation
for (i in 1:(length(numeric_columns) - 1)) {
  for (j in (i + 1):length(numeric_columns)) {
    if (all(c(numeric_columns[i], numeric_columns[j]) %in% colnames(data))) {
      s <- ggplot(data, aes(x = !!sym(numeric_columns[i]), y = !!sym(numeric_columns[j]), color = binaryClass)) +
        geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
        labs(title = paste("Scatterplot of", numeric_columns[i], "vs", numeric_columns[j])) +
        scale_color_manual(values = c("tan", "red")) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

      print(s)
    }
  }
}

# -------------------- Step 12: Visualize Outliers with Boxplots --------------------
# Plot boxplots for numeric variables to detect outliers
for (col in numeric_columns) {
  b <- ggplot(data, aes(y = !!sym(col))) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "grey", outlier.colour = "red", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(title = paste("Boxplot for", col), y = col) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(b)
}

# -------------------- Step 13: Replace Outliers with Median --------------------
replace_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1

  lower_bound <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
  upper_bound <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

  median_val <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  x <- ifelse(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound, median_val, x)

  return(x)
}

# Apply the function to each numeric column
for (col in numeric_columns) {
  data[[col]] <- replace_outliers(data[[col]])
}

summary(data)

cat("Cleaned dataset with outliers replaced by median values.\n")

# -------------------- Step 14: Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality --------------------
cat("\nShapiro-Wilk Test for Normality:\n")
for (col in numeric_columns) {
  p_value <- tryCatch({
    shapiro.test(data[[col]])$p.value
  }, error = function(e) NA)

  cat(col, ": p-value =", p_value, "\n")
}

# -------------------- Step 15: Chi-Square Test --------------------
chi_table <- table(data$sex, data$binaryClass)
chi_test <- chisq.test(chi_table)

cat("\nChi-Square Test between sex and binaryClass:\n")
print(chi_test)

# -------------------- Step 16: Mann-Whitney U Test --------------------
results <- list()

# Perform Mann-Whitney U Test for each numeric variable
for (var in numeric_columns) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste(var, "~ binaryClass"))
  test_result <- wilcox.test(formula, data = data, exact = FALSE)

  results[[var]] <- test_result
}

for (var in numeric_columns) {
  cat("Mann-Whitney U Test for", var, "\n")
  print(results[[var]])
  cat("\n")
}

# -------------------- Step 17: Correlation Heatmap --------------------
data_numeric <- data[numeric_columns]
cor_matrix <- cor(data_numeric, use = "complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, 
          hc.order = TRUE, 
          type = "lower", 
          lab = TRUE, 
          colors = c("blue", "white", "red"),
          title = "Heatmap of Correlations Among Numeric Predictors")

# -------------------- Step 18: Machine Learning Models --------------------
install.packages("caTools")
install.packages("randomForest")
library(caTools)
library(randomForest)

# Split the dataset into training and testing sets
set.seed(123)
split <- sample.split(data$binaryClass, SplitRatio = 0.8)

train_data <- subset(data, split == TRUE)
test_data <- subset(data, split == FALSE)

cat("\nNumber of rows in training dataset:", nrow(train_data))
cat("\nNumber of rows in testing dataset:", nrow(test_data))

# Fit a Logistic Regression Model
logistic_model <- glm(binaryClass ~ age + T3 + TSH + TT4 + FTI + sex, 
                      data = train_data, 
                      family = binomial)

cat("\nLogistic Regression Model Summary:\n")
summary(logistic_model)

logistic_preds <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
logistic_preds_class <- ifelse(logistic_preds > 0.5, 1, 0)

logistic_conf_matrix <- table(test_data$binaryClass, logistic_preds_class)
cat("\nConfusion Matrix for Logistic Regression:\n")
print(logistic_conf_matrix)

logistic_accuracy <- sum(diag(logistic_conf_matrix)) / sum(logistic_conf_matrix)
cat("\nAccuracy for Logistic Regression:", logistic_accuracy, "\n")

# Fit a Random Forest Model
random_forest_model <- randomForest(binaryClass ~ age + T3 + TSH + TT4 + FTI + sex, 
                                     data = train_data, 
                                     importance = TRUE, 
                                     ntree = 500)

cat("\nRandom Forest Model Summary:\n")
print(random_forest_model)

cat("\nVariable Importance:\n")
print(importance(random_forest_model))

rf_preds <- predict(random_forest_model, newdata = test_data)

rf_conf_matrix <- table(test_data$binaryClass, rf_preds)
cat("\nConfusion Matrix for Random Forest:\n")
print(rf_conf_matrix)

rf_accuracy <- sum(diag(rf_conf_matrix)) / sum(rf_conf_matrix)
cat("\nAccuracy for Random Forest:", rf_accuracy, "\n")
```
